text: On 22 October 2026, AAK convened its second partner workshop under the Kenya Decarbonization Finance Accelerator Programme, in collaboration with the Global Buildings Performance Network (GBPN). Held alongside the Urban Thinkers Campus (UTC) 10.0 under the theme “Housing Matters,” the workshop focused on “Financing the Green Transition for Adequate, Affordable and Climate-Resilient Housing.” Discussions explored financing barriers to sustainable construction, including limited access to appropriate financing, inadequate project preparation and challenges in developing bankable investments. Case studies highlighted the environmental, social and financial benefits of green buildings. Through two Action Labs, participants examined how built environment professionals can strengthen project design, reduce investment risks and improve bankability, before prioritizing scalable housing interventions, financing mechanisms and implementation pathways. The process aimed to inform a Housing Delivery and Finance Action Matrix to support the programme’s National Funding Strategy and Investment Prospectus. The workshop underscored the need for coordinated action among government, financial institutions, developers and built environment professionals to mobilize investment, accelerate sustainable construction and deliver adequate, affordable and climate-resilient housing in Kenya.
